title: Freva portal landing definition
description: One named landing: an ordered list of framework-owned block types carrying project-owned data.

layout.description: Lays the landing out on a 12-column grid. Without it, the landing keeps the design's composition.

intent.description: A typed action on an existing component: select-facet and open-dataset open the Data Browser with a SearchIntentV1; run-example opens the page that offers a registered example's run control.

dataset.description: A dataset identifier, searched as the Data Browser's free text.

example.description: A registered example id, as the build reports it (content:<page>#<n>).

notebook.description: The portal's notebook on `playgroundOrigin`: `lab` opens its JupyterLab interface (with the assistant and the data panel), `files` its file list. Requires `pythonPlayground.notebook.enabled`; `lab` also needs `notebook.assistant` or `notebook.dataPanel`.

section.description: The layout section this block belongs to (layout.sections).

span.description: Columns of the 12-column grid this block spans: below 768px (base), from 768px (md) and from 1100px (lg). Each defaults to the one before it, and base to 12.

figure.description: An illustration beside the text: the text in the first column, the figure in the second (below the text on a narrow screen). `image` is the still picture, shown when motion is reduced, before a video plays and without JavaScript; `video` (MP4 or WebM, muted, looping; a list gives the same clip in several formats) plays while the figure is on screen. `imageDark` and `videoDark` are the dark theme's. Every file must be inside a `rendering.assets` root, and is named relative to the landing file.

video.description: One file, or the same clip in several formats (MP4 and WebM): the browser plays the first it can.

videoDark.description: One file, or the same clip in several formats (MP4 and WebM): the browser plays the first it can.

blockNotebook.description: The portal's notebook, in the page: JupyterLite in a frame from `playgroundOrigin`, with Maximize (the page's own sheet, as the dataset browser has) and Open in a new tab above it. Requires `pythonPlayground.notebook.enabled`; `view: lab` also needs `notebook.assistant` or `notebook.dataPanel`. The notebook's policy then lets the portal's own origin, and only it, frame the notebook.

view.description: `lab` (default): the JupyterLab interface. `files`: the Notebook interface's file list.

title.description: The name on the notebook window's bar. Default: "<site title> Playground", the notebook's own tab title.

blockDatasetTree.description: A dataset archive, browsed in place. TWO SOURCE MODES, exactly one of which must be given. `catalog` is a build-time SNAPSHOT: a project-owned file validated and embedded while the artifact is produced, so the block issues no request at page load and depends on no service being up. `s3` is LIVE: the block lists one prefix of an S3-compatible gateway when a row is expanded, which is how a petabyte archive is browsed without a build that walks it. A live block adds the endpoint to the recorded `connect-src` and its contents depend on that gateway being up and CORS-readable; a snapshot block adds nothing and depends on nothing. It is a full-width landing block in the portal's normal content region: a hierarchy with descriptions, right-aligned metadata and an inline detail panel needs the page's width, not a hero column.

catalog.description: Path to a dataset-tree-catalog-v1 JSON document, relative to this landing file and inside the source root. Read at build time and embedded in the page; never fetched. Mutually exclusive with `s3`.

s3.description: Browse an S3-compatible gateway live, one prefix per expanded row. Mutually exclusive with `catalog`. THE ROOTS ARE DECLARED, never discovered: this never issues ListBuckets, because an S3 root legitimately answers 403 and a browser cannot be asked to enumerate someone's account. What a visitor can reach is what the deployment listed here.

endpoint.description: Absolute URL of the gateway, with no credentials and no query. Its ORIGIN is added to the artifact's recorded `connect-src`, and nothing else about the policy changes. HTTPS, except a loopback host over http for a development gateway. Checked by the build rather than by a pattern here: a block whose `type` is right and whose endpoint is a typo should be told which value is wrong and why, and a failed pattern inside a discriminated union reports every OTHER block type instead.

style.description: `path` puts the bucket in the URL path; `virtual-host` puts it in the hostname. Default `path`, which is what a self-hosted gateway serves and what needs no wildcard certificate.

roots.description: The buckets and prefixes this tree may browse. Required, and the whole of what is reachable.

id.description: Node identifier. Defaults to `s3://bucket/prefix`, which is already stable and unique.

prefix.description: Key prefix to start at. Must end with `/` when given, and must not start with one; the build says so by name rather than by a pattern here, so the message names the root that is wrong.

link.description: A project or documentation page for this collection, drawn as a small external-link control beside its title. Carried rather than derived: a URL invented from the bucket name would navigate a reader to a raw storage listing instead of a page written for them.

href.description: Absolute https URL. Checked by the build, which names the root that is wrong.

label.description: Accessible name for the link. Defaults to a generic one.

planned.description: Announced but not yet browsable, and the badge's exact text. The row is drawn with no chevron, no aria-expanded and no listing request - not on expansion, because there is none, and not on the background availability probe either.

maxKeys.description: Keys per request. Default 1000, the protocol maximum.

maxPages.description: Continuation pages per expansion. Default 25. Reaching it stops the walk and says so in the row; it is never a silent cut.

retries.description: Retries for network errors and 5xx only. Default 1. Never unbounded.

datasetSuffixes.description: Prefix suffixes that mark a chunked store rather than a directory - a `.zarr` prefix is one dataset, not a thousand chunk files, and the tree stops there. Default `[".zarr"]`.

searchIndex.description: A dataset-tree-search-index-v1 JSON document, relative to this landing file and inside the source root, that makes search over a LIVE (`s3`) tree cover the whole index rather than only the branches a visitor has opened. The build validates it and publishes it beside the pages as one content-hashed, same-origin file (`_portal/dataset-tree-index.<hash>.json`), listed in the manifests and in `checksums.sha256`; the page loads it after the tree has mounted and never waits for it, and a search makes no S3 request. Produced by the deployment (for example a scheduled job that lists the buckets); this build does not crawl. Valid only with `s3`: a `catalog` snapshot is complete, so the tree searches it whole and would ignore an index.

searchResultLimit.description: With `searchIndex`: how many search results are drawn before the rest are reported as a count. Default 200.

expand.description: Node identifiers to expand as soon as they appear, at any depth. In snapshot mode an identifier the catalogue does not contain is a build error rather than a silent no-op; in live mode the identifiers are `s3://bucket/prefix/` and cannot be checked at build time, because checking would mean listing the archive at build time - which is the thing live mode exists not to do.

statusLabel.description: Pill text for the footer status line. Defaults to SNAPSHOT for a build-time catalogue and LIVE for an S3 source, which is the honest word for each.

python.description: The optional in-page Python playground. Absent, or `enabled: false`, and the block is Copy-only: no interpreter chunk is loaded, no Worker or iframe is created, and the page's Content-Security-Policy is not widened. Turning it on adds a run control beside eligible examples in the catalogue and a terminal window to run them in.

enabled.description: The whole switch. Everything below is inert while this is false.

profile.description: Which browser-python profile the interpreter loads, e.g. `xarray-zarr`. Passed through verbatim: the set of profiles belongs to that package and a list here would go stale.

autostart.description: When the interpreter is brought up. `never` waits for the first run; `after-interactive` warms it once the page is idle; `immediately` starts it during load and is a deliberate cost on every visitor, including the ones who never press anything. Default `never`.

network.description: How much of the network this page's Python may reach. `origins` (the default) is the exact allowlist and nothing else, with a public package index refused wherever it is configured. `https` adds the `https:` SCHEME to `connect-src` - any TLS origin, never plaintext - which is what lets a visitor run `micropip.install("name")`, paste a wheel URL, or read a CORS-enabled dataset nobody listed at deployment time. The prepared environment is unchanged and is still the starting point. Choose it deliberately: an installed package runs in the same interpreter as the rest of the session. Add-ons are NOT configurable here - they belong to the portal-level `pythonPlayground` stanza, which is where the artefacts they need are resolved.

maxSessions.description: How many independent interpreters one page may hold. Two is the ceiling and not merely the default: each is a Worker with its own WASM heap, and the second one is created only after the visitor has been told what it costs.

initialSource.description: Python run once, into a new session, before anything the visitor asks for. Part of the portal's own configuration and therefore trusted exactly as much as the rest of it.

playgroundOrigin.description: Serve the interpreter from THIS origin, in a frame, instead of the portal's own. Recommended for a public deployment: visitor Python and anything it installs otherwise run with the portal's origin authority. An exact origin, never a wildcard and never a path. HTTPS, with one exception: a loopback host over http, because that is what a development server and an acceptance run are - and a browser already treats loopback as a secure context, so the interpreter's own WebAssembly and crypto requirements are met there. Any other http origin is refused.

runtimeIndexUrl.description: Fetch the Python runtime from THIS directory instead of the pinned CDN. A deployment that mirrors Pyodide - because its network does not reach a CDN, or because it will not depend on one - points this at its own copy, and the recorded Content-Security-Policy names that origin instead. Must end with a slash: it is a directory the interpreter resolves file names against, not a file. The version it serves must be the one this build pins; a different one is a runtime the console was not built for.

terminal.description: How the window around the console is drawn.

style.description: The only value, and it is spelled out rather than assumed so a second style can be added later without changing what an existing portal means.

osControls.description: Which window controls to draw. `auto` reads the visitor's platform.

alwaysOnTop.description: Keep the window above portal-owned content, including while minimized. It cannot cover browser-native surfaces - a file picker, a permission prompt, fullscreen UI - and does not claim to.

rememberAppearance.description: Persist the window's colour, opacity and text size in this browser.

section.description: The layout section this block belongs to (layout.sections).

span.description: Columns of the 12-column grid this block spans: below 768px (base), from 768px (md) and from 1100px (lg). Each defaults to the one before it, and base to 12.

flavourName.$comment: A flavour is a lens the DEPLOYMENT's own freva-rest instance serves, not a value this schema can know. The widget types it as a plain string for exactly that reason. Constrained to an identifier so a typo is still caught, but never to a fixed list - a portal whose backend serves `waterpark` must be able to name it.

background.description: none, the surface or accent fill, or a local image (published as a hashed file; never a URL).
